items.stem: Ingrid designs a kite-shaped logo ABCD with AB = AD and CB = CD. Angle BAD = 74° and angle BCD = 124°. (a) Explain why angles ABC and ADC are equal. (b) Find angle ABC. (c) The diagonal AC is drawn; find angle BAC and angle ACB and check the angle sum of triangle ABC.

items.markingKey: (a) the kite is symmetric about AC (triangles ABC and ADC are congruent, SSS) (b) 81° (c) BAC = 37°, ACB = 62°; 37 + 62 + 81 = 180. Angle facts stated (R1); calculation (M1 A1 A1); general reasoning communicated (C1).

items.stem: A field in Mumbai has the shape of an irregular polygon with 6 sides. A surveyor measures 5 of the interior angles as 145°, 121°, 159°, 145°, 133°. (a) Find the interior angle sum. (b) Find the remaining angle. (c) Find the exterior angle at that corner and explain what the surveyor could check using all the exterior angles.
items.answer: (a) 720° (b) 17° (c) 163°; the exterior angles must add up to 360°
items.markingKey: (a) 720° (b) 17° (c) 163°; the exterior angles must add up to 360°. Pattern described and generalised (B: M1 A1); formula applied (A1); justified conclusion (R1 C1).

items.stem: A triangular garden in Toronto has sides 8 m, 11 m and 12 m. (a) Choose a scale and describe how to construct an accurate scale drawing using ruler and compasses. (b) Check that the triangle can be made. (c) A tree is to be planted the same distance from all three corners – describe how to find its position.
items.answer: (a) e.g. 1 cm : 1 m; draw 12 cm, arcs of 8 cm and 11 cm from the ends (b) 8 + 11 = 19 > 12, so it exists (c) construct the perpendicular bisectors of two sides; the tree goes where they cross
items.markingKey: (a) e.g. 1 cm : 1 m; draw 12 cm, arcs of 8 cm and 11 cm from the ends (b) 8 + 11 = 19 > 12, so it exists (c) construct the perpendicular bisectors of two sides; the tree goes where they cross. Correct constructions/loci chosen (M1 A1); triangle inequality or intersection reasoning (R1); clear description of method (C1).

items.stem: An angle of 75° is formed by a transversal and one of two parallel lines. What is the size of its alternate angle?
items.markingKey: A. Alternate angles are equal.

items.stem: What is the complement of 37°?
Which term matches this description: "The interior angles of any triangle add up to 180°"?
items.answer: angle sum of a triangle
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of angle sum of a triangle.

items.stem: Explain whether regular triangles can tessellate (fit together around a point with no gaps), using the interior angle.
items.answer: Interior angle 60°; 360 ÷ 60 = 6, a whole number, so they tessellate.
items.markingKey: Interior angle found (A1); condition 360 ÷ interior angle must be a whole number (R1); conclusion (A1).

items.stem: Two mobile phone masts A and B are 11 km apart. Explain how to construct the set of points that are the same distance from both masts, and why your construction works.
items.answer: Construct the perpendicular bisector of AB; its points are equidistant from A and B because the equal compass arcs from A and B meet on it.
items.markingKey: Perpendicular bisector named (A1); construction steps (M1); reason (R1).

items.stem: Explain why co-interior angles between parallel lines add to 180°.
items.answer: One co-interior angle is equal to the corresponding angle of the other, which lies on a straight line with it; angles on a straight line add to 180°.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: One co-interior angle is equal to the corresponding angle of the other, which lies on a straight line with it; angles on a straight line add to 180°. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Tariq says: "Two lines cross making an angle of 62°, so the angle next to it is also 62° because they are vertically opposite." Explain the mistake.
items.answer: The angle next to it is adjacent, not vertically opposite; it is 180 − 62 = 118°. The angle opposite is 62°.
items.markingKey: Adjacent vs vertically opposite distinguished (R1); correct value (A1).

items.stem: In a triangle with interior angles 40°, 50° and c, show that the exterior angle next to c is equal to 40° + 50°. Explain why this is true for every triangle.
items.answer: c = 180 − 40 − 50 = 90°; exterior = 180 − c = 90° = 40 + 50. In general exterior = 180 − c = a + b because a + b + c = 180.
items.markingKey: Numerical demonstration (A1); general argument (R1 R1).

items.stem: Explain whether regular hexagons can tessellate (fit together around a point with no gaps), using the interior angle.
items.answer: Interior angle 120°; 360 ÷ 120 = 3, a whole number, so they tessellate.
items.markingKey: Interior angle found (A1); condition 360 ÷ interior angle must be a whole number (R1); conclusion (A1).

items.stem: Describe the steps to construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment AB of length 8 cm.
items.answer: Set compasses to more than 4 cm; draw arcs from A and from B above and below AB; join the two intersection points with a straight line.
items.markingKey: Set compasses to more than 4 cm; draw arcs from A and from B above and below AB; join the two intersection points with a straight line.

items.stem: A student claims: "Co-interior angles are equal." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Co-interior angles add up to 180°; they are equal only if both are 90°.
items.markingKey: Co-interior angles add up to 180°; they are equal only if both are 90°. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Two angles on a straight line are 2x° and (3x + 10)°. Find x and the size of each angle.
In triangle PQR, angle P = 77° and angle Q = 54°. Side QR is extended beyond R. Find the exterior angle at R and angle PRQ.
items.answer: exterior 131°, angle PRQ = 49°
items.markingKey: Exterior angle = 77 + 54 = 131° (A1 R1); interior 49° (A1).

items.stem: Find the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon.
Describe how to construct an angle of 60° at point P on a line.
items.answer: With centre P draw an arc crossing the line at Q; with the same radius and centre Q draw an arc crossing the first arc at R; join PR: angle RPQ = 60°.
items.markingKey: With centre P draw an arc crossing the line at Q; with the same radius and centre Q draw an arc crossing the first arc at R; join PR: angle RPQ = 60°.

items.stem: Lines AB and CD are parallel, and a transversal meets them at P and Q. Angle APQ = 38°. Find angle PQD, explaining each step.
items.markingKey: Angle APQ and angle PQD are alternate angles (R1), so angle PQD = 38° (A1).

items.stem: Around a point there are angles x°, 6x°, (x + 24)° and (2x − 24)°. (a) Form an equation. (b) Solve it for x. (c) Find the size of each angle and check they add to 360°.
items.markingKey: (a) x + 6x + x + 24 + 2x − 24 = 360 (b) x = 36 (c) 36°, 216°, 60°, 48°. Angle fact used to form an equation (M1 A1); solved (A1); all angles found and checked (A1 C1).

items.stem: Kenji designs a kite-shaped logo ABCD with AB = AD and CB = CD. Angle BAD = 79° and angle BCD = 98°. (a) Explain why angles ABC and ADC are equal. (b) Find angle ABC. (c) The diagonal AC is drawn; find angle BAC and angle ACB and check the angle sum of triangle ABC.
items.answer: (a) the kite is symmetric about AC (triangles ABC and ADC are congruent, SSS) (b) 91.5° (c) BAC = 39.5°, ACB = 49°; 39.5 + 49 + 91.5 = 180
items.markingKey: (a) the kite is symmetric about AC (triangles ABC and ADC are congruent, SSS) (b) 91.5° (c) BAC = 39.5°, ACB = 49°; 39.5 + 49 + 91.5 = 180. Angle facts stated (R1); calculation (M1 A1 A1); general reasoning communicated (C1).

items.stem: A designer in Mexico City makes a floor pattern with a regular octagon and squares. (a) Find the interior angle of a regular octagon. (b) Show that two octagons and one square fit exactly around a point. (c) Explain why regular pentagons cannot be used alone. (d) Find the exterior angle of a regular 10-gon.
items.answer: (a) 135° (b) 135 + 135 + 90 = 360° (c) the interior angle 108° does not divide 360 exactly (d) 36°
items.markingKey: (a) 135° (b) 135 + 135 + 90 = 360° (c) the interior angle 108° does not divide 360 exactly (d) 36°. Pattern described and generalised (B: M1 A1); formula applied (A1); justified conclusion (R1 C1).
